[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Collections, Folders, and Request Organization in Postman"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"As your API testing workspace grows, managing dozens or hundreds of individual requests becomes challenging. Postman provides a hierarchical structure using Collections and Folders to keep your API projects organized, shareable, and scalable."},{"order":3,"type":"heading","text":"Understanding Collections"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"A collection is a top-level container that groups related API requests together. Think of it as a project directory. Collections allow you to execute entire workflows, manage shared variables, configure authentication, and run automated tests."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Key Features of Collections"},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Authorization: Set authorization credentials at the collection level, which inherited by all child requests."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Variables: Define collection-level variables for environments, tokens, and base URLs."},{"order":8,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Scripts: Run pre-request scripts and tests across all requests inside the collection."},{"order":9,"type":"heading","text":"Structuring with Folders"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inside collections, you can create folders to further categorize your requests. Folders help mimic the structure of your backend architecture (e.g., separating endpoints by resource like Users, Auth, and Payments)."},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Example Directory Structure"},{"order":12,"type":"code","text":"E-Commerce API (Collection)
├── Auth (Folder)
│   ├── POST /login
│   └── POST /refresh-token
├── Users (Folder)
│   ├── GET /users
│   └── PUT /users/:id
└── Payments (Folder)
    └── POST /checkout"},{"order":13,"type":"heading","text":"Best Practices for Request Organization"},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Descriptive Naming: Prefix requests with HTTP methods (e.g., "GET - Fetch User Details") for quick scanning."},{"order":15,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Leverage Inheritance: Apply authorization and headers at the collection level instead of repeating them in every request."},{"order":16,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Export and Backup: Regularly export your collections as JSON files or sync them with a Postman Team Workspace for collaboration."}]
